requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as the managed systemd service inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: The installed unit uses the required executable. It was enabled and active, with a live worker process in inventory-worker.service's cgroup both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configure inventory-worker to start automatically during boot.
requirements.summary: A complete boot transition was observed: healthy enabled/active baseline, acknowledged reboot, temporary loss of connectivity, changed boot identity, and automatic recovery as an enabled active service. The new-boot journal records systemd starting the unit.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The worker is managed by inventory-worker.service, and direct reboot testing proves it starts automatically on a new boot. The mandatory node-restart evidence is strong and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: The node-wide systemd state was degraded before and after execution because ssh.service was already failed. Thus the restart protocol does not demonstrate a globally healthy systemd state, although it directly demonstrates healthy task-service state and recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The temporary discovery file created by cmd-e49397dc7d7b45b4 supported checking for an existing unit and did not remain after reboot. cmd-f4eab50408f54b73 installed and validated the required unit and cleaned its temporary source file; cmd-7f3c0c3ed94942d6 enabled and started it; cmd-114c60f8a136435d performed the required bounded reboot verification. No abandoned executor temporary files, damaged package state, task-related failed units, or unsafe worker listeners are evident. The ssh.service failure existed before execution and remained unchanged.
